newsitem.title: GREECE: DRACHMA ATTRACTIVE WITH ECU/DR OVER 310-BANKAMERICA.
newsitem.headline: DRACHMA ATTRACTIVE WITH ECU/DR OVER 310-BANKAMERICA.

text.p: Ecu/drachma was seen locked in the 307-313 range in the next two months but at rates above 310 it offered good drachma buying opportunities, said Bank of America in its June-July bond strategy report.

"The ecu/drachma rate is expected to fluctuate in the 307-313 range and mark/drachma in the range of 155-160 in the next two months," it said. "We also consider ecu/drachma rates above the 310 level as good drachma buying opportunities."

The rise of the ecu versus the drachma is a demonstration of the pursued increase in short-term volatility rather than a deviation from the central bank's hard drachma policy, said Bank of America in its report on Italy, Spain and Greece.

It is unlikely that the central bank will devalue the drachma despite the increasing external imbalances because structural reforms had yet to be implemented and local firms having resorted to forex funding would be harmed, it said.
"It is therefore doubtful that Bank of Greece will take such an initiative before it is time to join the ERM-2, that is in the beginning of 1999," it said.
Discount margins on six-and seven-year FRNs will remain relatively stable, around 40 basis points in the next two months, with a small correction in FRN prices possible in the next two months.
Discount or effective margin is the average spread over the reference rate that investors expect to earn over the life of the security.

The report said headline inflation overestimated the actual pace of CPI deceleration and pointed to the widening gap between headline inflation, 5.9 percent year-on-year in April, and core inflation, 7.5 percent in the same month, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
